title: Weather, Climate & Disaster Overlay Library
source_and_design_basis: ENV-04_OVERLAY_MODEL_v1.0.0.json overlay definition, relation, intensity, effect-key and deterministic-resolution contract
ENV-05 through ENV-10 preset trait/hint records that deferred weather, hydrology, ecological and geologic conditions
library_rules: An overlay is a reusable environmental delta, never a base environment identity.
No overlay automatically activates another overlay; causal activation remains GM, authored-event, scenario, or separately governed runtime authority.
Relations apply only when both referenced overlays are active in materially overlapping scopes.
ENV-04 intensity bands are semantic unless a source or local profile supplies an explicit mapping.
No universal movement, damage, endurance, exposure, structural, weather, or disaster formulas are invented here.
Stable effect keys deduplicate equivalent contributions while preserving unrelated effects and provenance.
All ENV-11 definitions are owner-authorized content design and do not claim recovered source text.

overlays.name: Heavy Rain
overlays.applicability: Atmosphere or medium capable of liquid precipitation.

deltas.value_or_reference: dense rainfall reduces visibility according to local intensity
elevated surface-water input and runoff
wet, slick, muddy, or waterlogged route complications where substrate permits
cover and drainage become more consequential

overlays.name: Monsoon Regime
overlays.applicability: Active seasonal monsoon regime; permanent climate classification remains preset/local parameterization.

deltas.value_or_reference: monsoon-season water-input and drainage-pressure regime
seasonally reduced route reliability where local drainage/substrate is vulnerable
seasonal surface-water availability may increase where locally supported

overlays.name: Fog
overlays.applicability: Medium and local conditions capable of ordinary suspended condensate or fog.

deltas.value_or_reference: distance/detail visibility reduced
visual route references become less reliable
visual discovery and approach context is obscured

overlays.name: Thunderstorm
overlays.applicability: Atmosphere or medium capable of ordinary convective storm behavior; rainfall may be separately represented.

deltas.value_or_reference: lightning/electrical-strike hazard present
rapid light and visibility variability from storm cells
gusts complicate exposed movement

overlays.name: Heavy Snow
overlays.applicability: Conditions capable of frozen precipitation; thermal enabling conditions remain base/local or ENV-12 authority.

deltas.value_or_reference: snow accumulation alters exposed surfaces
dense snowfall reduces visibility
snow cover obscures routes and complicates travel

overlays.name: Blizzard
overlays.applicability: Snow available for active snowfall or transport plus strong wind; thermal enabling conditions remain external.

deltas.value_or_reference: wind-driven snowfall/drift accumulation
severe snow/wind obscuration including whiteout where intensity supports
high wind complicates exposed movement and route keeping
combined wind and snow increase shelter dependence

overlays.name: Windstorm / Gale
overlays.applicability: Medium capable of significant ordinary wind or atmospheric flow.

deltas.value_or_reference: exposed travel/balance/route choice complicated by high wind
windborne debris/falling-object hazard where material is available
exposed water surfaces become wind-driven/rough where applicable

overlays.name: Hurricane / Cyclone
overlays.applicability: Ordinary atmosphere and storm context capable of a large rotating cyclone.

deltas.value_or_reference: widespread severe wind complicates exposed movement
rain bands and spray reduce visibility
storm rainfall can add substantial runoff where precipitation reaches the scope
widespread debris/falling-object hazard

overlays.name: Tornado
overlays.applicability: Atmosphere and storm context capable of a localized rotating vortex.

deltas.value_or_reference: localized extreme wind makes exposed movement highly unstable
localized high-energy debris hazard
ordinary shelter may be inadequate within the vortex path depending on construction

overlays.name: Sandstorm / Dust Storm
overlays.applicability: Loose sand, dust, or particulate material plus sufficient wind; not limited to desert presets.

deltas.value_or_reference: airborne sand/dust reduces visibility
airborne mineral particulate load elevated
route finding and landmark use complicated
abrasive particulate exposure where unprotected

overlays.name: Hailstorm
overlays.applicability: Atmospheric storm conditions capable of hail formation.

deltas.value_or_reference: falling hail impact hazard according to local intensity
temporary hail accumulation may alter exposed surfaces
exposed vegetation/crops may be damaged where locally applicable

overlays.name: Flood
overlays.applicability: Water source or local condition capable of inundating normally exposed terrain or structures; Floodplain/Flooded Forest identity alone does not activate Flood.

deltas.value_or_reference: water occupies normally exposed terrain/structures according to local depth/extent
routes/crossings/ground travel altered by standing or moving floodwater
low-lying shelter/access may be lost or degraded
stored/local resources may become inaccessible, damaged, or contaminated where supported

overlays.name: Flash Flood
overlays.applicability: Terrain or drainage capable of rapid concentrated flow.

deltas.value_or_reference: rapid temporary inundation along affected flow paths
fast-moving floodwater/torrent condition
crossings/routes can become abruptly hazardous or unusable
debris/scour/impact hazards may accompany rapid flow

overlays.name: Drought
overlays.applicability: Sustained water deficit relative to a local baseline; arid presets do not automatically imply Drought.

deltas.value_or_reference: surface/accessible water availability reduced relative to local baseline
soils/vegetation/fuels become unusually dry where applicable
water-dependent local resources become less reliable

overlays.name: Storm Surge
overlays.applicability: Coast, shore, estuary, large open-water margin, or other water body capable of wind/pressure-driven level rise.

deltas.value_or_reference: temporary wind/pressure-driven water-level rise
surge-associated wave/current energy elevated
shore/coastal routes and access points may flood or become wave-swept

overlays.name: Tsunami / Seiche
overlays.applicability: Sufficiently large water body and separately established triggering context; ENV-11 does not infer the trigger.

deltas.value_or_reference: large transient displacement/oscillation changes water levels
high-energy surge/wave/current condition
debris/scour/impact hazard where material is present
shoreline/harbor/low-route access may change abruptly

overlays.name: Wildfire
overlays.applicability: Burnable fuel and conditions supporting combustion; vegetation-rich or drought conditions do not automatically activate Wildfire.

deltas.value_or_reference: active flame/heat/fire-front hazard where burning
smoke and combustion particulate load elevated in affected/downwind scope
smoke obscures visibility where present
active fire/heat/smoke/falling material can close or redirect routes
exposed biological/material resources may be consumed or damaged

overlays.name: Volcanic Ash
overlays.applicability: Airborne ash established near or far from an eruption; active Volcanic Eruption need not remain active.

deltas.value_or_reference: volcanic particulate load elevated
airborne ash reduces visibility/light penetration
ash accumulates on exposed surfaces
exposed water/food/material resources may be fouled by ash

overlays.name: Volcanic Eruption
overlays.applicability: Separately established active volcanic/geothermal source; a Volcano preset does not automatically imply eruption.

deltas.value_or_reference: active eruptive hazards such as lava, pyroclastic, ballistic, vent, or ground-instability phenomena as locally established
terrain can be altered/blocked by eruptive deposits or flows where present
routes can be blocked or redirected by active eruptive zones

overlays.name: Earthquake
overlays.applicability: Separately established seismic/tectonic or analogous ordinary physical cause; no supernatural cause is inferred.

deltas.value_or_reference: ground motion/local surface disruption according to intensity
routes/crossings/structures may become unstable or blocked as locally supported
falling-object/structural-collapse hazard where unstable material exists

overlays.name: Avalanche
overlays.applicability: Slope and unstable snow, ice, or debris mantle capable of rapid downslope movement; Highland/Ice Mass alone does not activate Avalanche.

deltas.value_or_reference: rapid downslope snow/ice/debris burial and impact hazard
routes/crossings may be buried, cut, or redirected
fresh avalanche deposit alters local surface

overlays.name: Landslide / Mudslide
overlays.applicability: Slope, bank, cut, fill, or unstable material capable of downslope movement; Heavy Rain/Earthquake may contribute only when separately active.

deltas.value_or_reference: rapid soil/rock/debris movement, burial, and impact hazard
routes/channels/access points may be blocked or redirected
fresh slide/debris deposits alter local terrain
slides may block/divert channels where they intersect watercourses

authored_cross_overlay_relations.note: If both are active, monsoon regime can increase persistence/recurrence context; it does not create Heavy Rain.
If both are active, rainfall can add water input; it does not create Flood.
If both are active on susceptible terrain, saturation can increase instability.
Rain reaching burning fuels can reduce spread/persistence but does not guarantee extinguishment.
Cyclone wind/pressure can increase separately active surge severity.
Dry fuels can increase separately active Wildfire spread/persistence.
An ash-producing eruption can increase separately active Volcanic Ash.
Seismic ground motion can increase a separately active slope failure.

explicit_non_causation_examples: Heavy Rain does not automatically activate Flood or Flash Flood.
Monsoon Regime does not automatically activate Heavy Rain at every moment.
Thunderstorm does not automatically activate Heavy Rain or Hailstorm.
Hurricane/Cyclone does not automatically activate Storm Surge, Flood, or Tornado.
Drought does not automatically activate Wildfire.
Earthquake does not automatically activate Landslide or Tsunami/Seiche.
Volcanic Eruption does not automatically activate the separate Volcanic Ash overlay.
Blizzard does not automatically activate Avalanche.
